Today’s software development and engineering teams waste hours of valuable time and resources waiting on pipeline builds, only to scramble to find a solution when one breaks. To mitigate this frustrating and time consuming cycle, Harness enhanced its marquee open source CI module, with a series of updates that allow developers to quickly respond to failures and create a shorter path back to innovation. Rebranded as Harness CI Community Edition, if a build does break, the developer is now presented with a link to the failed CI server allowing them to debug with ease. About Harness

Based in San Francisco, Harness is the only end-to-end platform for complete software delivery designed to provide a simple, safe and secure way for engineering and DevOps teams to release applications into production. Harness uses machine learning to detect the quality of deployments and automatically roll back failed ones, saving time and reducing the need for custom scripting and manual oversight. Harness customers include NCR, Kohl’s, Discover Financial, Nationwide Insurance and McAfee. Follow Harness on Twitter or try Harness for free at harness.io.

results.title: HAR: Open Source harness for multi-agent coding workflows
results.content:
Viktor.com

What do you think? …

Antoine Frau
HAR

HAR

Hey PH!   
  
I’m Antoine, and over the past year, as I tried to scale our agentic coding workflows and software factories at my company, I kept hitting the same set of problems. So I built HAR to solve them, and I'm open sourcing it today.

Getting a single coding agent to work in a repo is easy. Scaling to a real multi-agent workflow, where several runs at once and you still trust the output, is where it breaks down. A few things go wrong at the same time:

No standard way to run or verify a repo. That knowledge is scattered across a README, a CLAUDE.md, editor rules, and CI config, all drifting out of sync with each other and the actual code. [...] All of this lives in one contract committed to your repo, which every agent reads the same way. It replaces the usual scatter of a README, a CLAUDE.md, editor rules, and CI config that drift apart. You start from a profile that matches your stack, your agent adapts it to the real repo, and you extend verification with plugins (like Playwright) or with any command you already run.

Give it a try and let me know what you think :)

I'd genuinely love feedback, especially from anyone already trying to run multiple agents in parallel. [...] Agents on one repo collide. Shared dev server, shared database, shared ports, conflicting git state.

Trusting a change means re-verifying it yourself. Which defeats the point of running a fleet.

Vendor sandboxes lock you in. If the setup lives in someone's hosted dashboard, switching agents later means rebuilding the whole thing.

What HAR does

HAR is a CLI and an MCP server. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any MCP agent, and it closes each of those gaps:

Isolation. Each agent gets its own git worktree, branch, ports, and database. Nothing is shared with the main checkout or another agent's slot, so a fleet runs in parallel without colliding on a dev server, DB, or ports.

We’re thrilled to announce the launch of Harness Open Source, the open-source edition of our enterprise platform. With Harness Open Source, developers can configure their cloud development environments, manage code repositories, build, test, deploy, and manage artifacts—all from a small DigitalOcean droplet or a laptop and with a single docker command. With this new open source offering, we aim to extend these benefits to all software development teams, regardless of size or budget, and continue our commitment to open source endeavors.

Developers must often juggle multiple tools to set up development environments, manage code, build/deploy pipelines, and manage artifacts. Onboarding these tools and maintaining them is a huge pain.

Harness Open Source offers developers a unified solution, eliminating the need to juggle multiple disjointed tools.
